page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 3800 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 128256.4 and a passmark CPU physics score in the top 10%. Memory performance is highly efficient, achieving a top-tier read-only small block bandwidth of 9194.14 GB/sec and strong large-block read and write speeds. Database and caching operations are highly optimized, as evidenced by a top-tier passmark database score and 181.85 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Single-threaded compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier.

The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. However, the lack of AVX, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets represents a tradeoff for workloads relying on legacy x86 vector extensions. This instance is highly suited for high-throughput database operations, static web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring fast local NVMe storage.
